note: The numbers of the cameras' look (kitchen_render.py beside this file). The room bundle (KITCHEN_RENDER_DIR) holds the room's meshes, textures and materials and the two panoramas; the rest is here. Units: the image light multiplies the panorama (path tracer W/m2/sr, x 683 -> cd/m2); the lamps are in candela from their lumens (kitchen_scene.lights()); exposure_scale multiplies every light and the image light (a camera exposure relative to Filament's default EV100 15); emissive values are Filament material emission (not scaled by exposure_scale).
white_balance_note: the display's white balance as linear gains per channel (the references' AgX view at 3863 K / tint -10.2: a warm input r/g 1.576, b/g 0.566 comes out neutral): baked into ibl.ktx and sky.ktx, and applied here to the lamps and the headlight; emitters (burners, indicators) are not balanced

ibl.panorama: the mean of three OVRTX path-traced probes at the work area (robot, unit and dressing hidden; all of the task's lights on; Blender scene-linear = HdrColor / 0.939), 128 px cube map by Filament's cmgen. ibl.ktx: the reflections from that mean, the diffuse light (its spherical harmonics) from the same mean with the lamps that are not drawn painted in as 5-degree disks carrying their direct light at the probe points; sky.ktx (behind the windows) from the mean

lamps.key_shadow_note: true: the key lamp casts PCF shadows; on 4 CPUs that adds about 50 ms to a fixed camera's image and 45 ms to a wrist image
lamps.drawn_note: the lamps drawn as Filament lights; the others (ceiling spots, pendants, shelf and under-cabinet LEDs) are in the image light's diffuse part (each lamp costs per-pixel time)

room.tint_note: linear per-channel gains per material name prefix (textures: applied to the texture), fitted so that each class's mean linear colour matches the path-traced references over 12 home states x 3 cameras

dressing.tint_note: linear per-channel gains per material name prefix (textures: applied to the texture), fitted so that each class's mean linear colour matches the path-traced references over 12 home states x 3 cameras

model_materials.tint_note: linear gains on the unit's (u_) and the robot's (r_) materials, same fit

burner_fx.note: the burners' visuals (kitchen_fx.py: gas = a ring of blue flame jets, glass-ceramic = the zone glowing under the glass, with a clear glossy coat over the glass top): emissive_gain scales the sheath, haze and glow emission of kitchen_fx.materials(), gas_inner_gain the inner cones' unlit colour; gas_buckets = level steps of the gas flames' shape
burner_fx.gain_note: emissive_gain and gas_inner_gain 0.22: the display's exposure (+2.55 EV in the colour grading) would otherwise wash the zones' red / orange and the flames out

indicator.note: a lit indicator glows with emissive_on in its own colour, made more saturated by lit_saturation (linear, about the luminance) ahead of the display's desaturation; off it is off_srgb (dark grey) like the model's

contact_shadows.note: static soft shadows: black decals (a black metal: no diffuse, no specular) that darken by alpha and fade out over margin_m (9-slice quads, process-cached meshes): the unit's footprint on its support (front = model -y; margins x clip(height / full_height_m, min_scale, 1)), the station's, the fillers' and the pedestal's footprints on the floor, the wall under the shelf; power = the falloff's exponent

hand_shadow.note: a soft blob per caster (robot body, radius m) straight below it on the unit's top or the support's top: alpha fades to 0 at fade_height_m above the plane, the radius grows by spread x height and stops at the plane's edge; alpha_buckets materials; drawn after the glass coat (blend_order)

filament_note: the display transform: filmic tone mapping with exposure, contrast, saturation and curves (shadow gamma, mid point, highlight scale) fitted to the references' display images (AgX Base Contrast) on 8 home states x 3 cameras: per-class mean colours and per-image luminance quantiles
episode_tint_note: episode_tint_in_grading: the episode's tint (appliance_env._appearance) is a per-channel gain in the colour grading (filament.cg.offset = log2(tint) / 17.52), so it reaches the image light too, whose colour MuJoCo 3.16's binding ignores; the lamps and the headlight then carry the white balance only
